items.value: The Butler Committee (Indian States Committee, 1927) was appointed to examine the relationship between the Paramount Power and the Indian princely States
items.reasoning: The Indian States Committee of 1927, chaired by Sir Harcourt Butler, was appointed to inquire into the relationship between the Paramount Power and the Indian (princely) States and to recommend how that relationship should be conducted; it reported in 1929. Option D is the only one that touches the princely States at all. Option A describes the concern of the constitutional reform debates and later the Government of India Act, 1935; option B relates to the India Office and not to Butler; option C describes press legislation such as the Vernacular Press Act. Note the stem's phrase 'Government of India' is a loose rendering of the Crown as Paramount Power, but D remains the intended and only defensible answer.

items.value: Domestic Content Requirement refers to the rule requiring solar power developers to use domestically manufactured cells and modules under India's solar mission
items.reasoning: Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) clauses in the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission obliged selected solar developers to source solar cells and modules manufactured in India. The United States challenged these clauses at the WTO as discriminatory against imported equipment, and the dispute panel and Appellate Body ruled against India in 2016, which is why the term was repeatedly in the news. The other options relate to broadcasting policy, agricultural export standards and higher-education FDI, none of which uses this term.

items.value: Both statements are wrong: the Nuclear Security Summits were a US-initiated process outside the UN, and the International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent expert group, not an IAEA organ
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Nuclear Security Summits (Washington 2010, Seoul 2012, The Hague 2014, Washington 2016) were launched on the initiative of the United States and ran as a stand-alone leaders' process, not under the aegis of the United Nations. Statement 2 is incorrect: the International Panel on Fissile Materials is an independent group of arms-control and non-proliferation experts, hosted at Princeton University, and has no institutional link to the International Atomic Energy Agency. With both statements false the answer is D.

items.value: State government employees who join service after their own State notifies the scheme are covered by the NPS
items.reasoning: The National Pension System was extended to State government employees State by State, each State applying it to employees recruited after the date of its own notification, so option C is correct. Option A is wrong because Non-Resident Indians may also join NPS, not only resident citizens. Option B is wrong because the entry age band is 18 to 60 years (later widened), not 21 to 55. Option D is wrong on two counts: the mandatory central-government coverage applies to those joining on or after 1 January 2004, and personnel of the Armed Forces are expressly excluded from it.

items.value: Only statement 2 is correct: the Rangeet rises in Sikkim and is a tributary of the Teesta; the Teesta does not share the Brahmaputra's source and does not reach the Bay of Bengal directly
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Teesta rises from the Tso Lhamo lake and Zemu glacier area in North Sikkim, whereas the Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) rises from the Chemayungdung/Angsi glacier region near Mansarovar in Tibet, so their sources are quite different. Statement 2 is correct: the Rangeet (Rangit) rises in western Sikkim and joins the Teesta near Melli on the Sikkim-West Bengal border. Statement 3 is incorrect: after entering Bangladesh the Teesta joins the Brahmaputra/Jamuna near Chilmari, so it is a tributary and does not itself debouch into the Bay of Bengal. Only statement 2 stands, giving B.

items.value: Both statements are correct: Zika is spread in the tropics by Aedes aegypti, the dengue vector, and sexual transmission of Zika is documented
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: in tropical regions the principal vector of Zika virus is Aedes aegypti, the same day-biting mosquito that transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever. Statement 2 is also correct: Zika is unusual among mosquito-borne flaviviruses in that it persists in semen and can be transmitted sexually, which is why health advisories issued during the 2015-16 outbreak covered sexual as well as vector transmission. Both being true, the answer is C.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the BIS Standard Mark is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes, while AGMARK is issued by India's Directorate of Marketing and Inspection, not by the FAO
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: pneumatic tyres and tubes for motor vehicles fall under the list of products for which BIS certification (the ISI mark) is compulsory, on safety grounds. Statement 2 is incorrect: AGMARK is a certification mark for agricultural produce issued under the Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection in the Union Ministry of Agriculture; the Food and Agriculture Organisation is a UN body and issues no such national mark. Hence A.

items.value: Both statements are correct: eNAM is a pan-India electronic trading portal for agricultural commodities, and it is designed to give farmers access to a nationwide market with quality-linked prices
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the National Agriculture Market (eNAM) is precisely a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks existing APMC mandis into a single online market. Statement 2 is also correct and is the scheme's central promise: by combining online bidding across a nationwide pool of buyers with assaying facilities at the mandi, it aims to give the farmer a wider market and a price that reflects the assessed quality of the produce rather than a local buyer's estimate. The runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if 'advantage' is read strictly, since statement 1 is a description of what the scheme IS rather than a benefit it delivers; for B to be correct the examiner would have to be enforcing that feature-versus-benefit distinction, which UPSC often does not.

items.value: Both statements are correct: the National IPR Policy affirms India's commitment to the Doha Development Agenda and TRIPS, and DIPP is the nodal agency for intellectual property in India
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the National Intellectual Property Rights Policy, 2016 explicitly reaffirms India's commitment to the Doha Development Round declaration on TRIPS and public health, and states that India's IP regime is fully TRIPS-compliant. Statement 2 is correct as the policy itself frames it: the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion was designated the nodal department to coordinate, guide and oversee implementation of the policy, and administration of the Copyright Act was moved to DIPP in 2016 to consolidate IP under one department. The runner-up is A (1 only), which would win if 'regulating' is read strictly, because DIPP is not the regulator for every IP right: plant varieties sit with the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority under the Agriculture Ministry, and semiconductor layout designs with MeitY.

items.value: All three - gharial, Indian wild ass and wild buffalo - are Schedule I animals that may not be hunted except as the Act allows
items.reasoning: Section 9 of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 prohibits hunting of animals specified in the Schedules, subject only to the narrow exceptions in sections 11 and 12 (danger to human life, disease, education and scientific research, and the like). The gharial, the Indian wild ass of the Rann of Kutch and the wild buffalo are all listed in Schedule I, which carries the highest level of protection and the severest penalties. Since all three are covered, the answer is D.

items.value: Neither statement is true: no process has been provided in the Constitution to enforce the Fundamental Duties, and they are moral and civic obligations rather than correlatives of legal duties
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is incorrect: Part IVA lays down the Fundamental Duties but the Constitution provides no mechanism for their enforcement, and unlike the Fundamental Rights they are non-justiciable; whether Parliament may legislate to give effect to some of them is a separate question from whether such a process 'has been provided'. Statement 2 is incorrect as commonly understood: the Fundamental Duties are moral and civic obligations addressed to the citizen, not the correlatives of enforceable legal duties. The runner-up is B (2 only), which would win if the examiner had in mind that some duties do have legal counterparts in existing statutes, such as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 for respecting the National Flag and Anthem, or environmental legislation for the duty to protect the environment - a link the Verma Committee (1999) drew explicitly.

items.value: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct; Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association, not the Madras Mahajana Sabha
items.reasoning: Pair 1 is correct: the British Indian Association was founded at Calcutta in 1851 with Raja Radhakanta Deb as its first President and Debendranath Tagore as Secretary. Pair 2 is wrong: Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association in 1852 and the newspaper Crescent; the Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded in 1884 by M. Viraraghavachariar, G. Subramania Iyer and P. Anandacharlu. Pair 3 is correct: the Indian Association was founded at Calcutta in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee along with Anandamohan Bose. Hence 1 and 3 only.

items.value: Economic liberty is not in the Preamble; the Preamble secures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and economic justice rather than economic liberty
items.reasoning: The Preamble resolves to secure to all citizens 'JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity'. Liberty is therefore promised in five named forms - thought, expression, belief, faith and worship - which covers options A, C and D. The word 'economic' appears in the Preamble only as a qualifier of justice, never of liberty, so economic liberty is the objective not embodied in it and B is the answer.

items.value: Both statements are correct: QCI was set up jointly by the Government of India and Indian industry, and its Chairman is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendation of industry
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Quality Council of India was established in 1997 as an autonomous body set up jointly by the Government of India and the Indian industry, represented by the three apex chambers ASSOCHAM, CII and FICCI, and it is registered as a society. Statement 2 follows QCI's own description of its governance: the Chairman of QCI is appointed by the Prime Minister on the recommendation of the industry to the Government, an arrangement that reflects the joint public-private character of the body. The runner-up is A (1 only), which would win if the appointment is in fact made by the administrative ministry (DIPP) rather than the Prime Minister, or if 'on the recommendations of the industry' overstates the industry's formal role - this is the statement a reviewer should verify first.

items.value: Only 1 and 2: Small Finance Banks exist to supply credit to small business units and to small and marginal farmers; encouraging young rural entrepreneurs is not among their stated objectives
items.reasoning: The RBI's guidelines state the objectives of Small Finance Banks as furthering financial inclusion by providing savings vehicles to unserved and underserved sections and by supplying credit to small business units, small and marginal farmers, micro and small industries and other unorganised sector entities, through high-technology low-cost operations. Statements 1 and 2 are lifted almost verbatim from that clause and are correct. Statement 3 is not in the objectives: the target group is defined by size and by exclusion from formal credit, not by the borrower's age, and the mandate is not confined to rural areas. The runner-up is D (1, 2 and 3), which would win if the examiner treated 'young entrepreneurs in rural areas' as an acceptable paraphrase of micro and small enterprises in unserved regions rather than as an added condition.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct: the first APMCHUD was held in New Delhi in 2006 on that theme, but India does not host all the conferences and they are not annual
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the first Asia Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development was hosted by India at New Delhi in December 2006 on the theme of emerging urban forms, policy responses and governance structures. Statement 2 is incorrect on two counts: later conferences were hosted by other countries - Iran (2008), the Republic of Korea (2010), Jordan (2012) and again Korea (2014) - so India does not host them all, and the conferences are held roughly every two years rather than annually. The claimed partnership with ADB, APEC and ASEAN is also not the organising arrangement. Hence A.

items.value: Democracy's superior virtue is that it calls into activity the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women
items.reasoning: This is the classic liberal-democratic argument, associated with John Stuart Mill and restated by Harold Laski: the merit of democracy is not that it produces the most expert or the swiftest government, but that participation develops the civic intelligence and moral character of ordinary citizens. Options B, C and D each point the other way - to executive strength, to a heroic individual leader and to party cadres respectively - which are the very concentrations of authority that democratic theory contrasts itself against.

items.value: UPI makes mobile wallets unnecessary for online payments, since money moves directly between bank accounts
items.reasoning: The Unified Payments Interface lets a user push or pull funds directly between bank accounts from a smartphone using a virtual payment address, with no need to pre-load money into an intermediary wallet, so option A is the direct and most likely consequence. Option B is speculation about the disappearance of cash that the interface itself cannot deliver. Option C confuses a domestic retail payments rail with foreign investment policy. Option D is wrong because direct benefit transfer already runs on the Aadhaar Payment Bridge and core banking, and does not depend on UPI.

items.value: These are terms from cosmology and particle physics, used in observing and understanding the Universe
items.reasoning: An event horizon is the boundary of a black hole beyond which nothing can escape, and a singularity is the point of infinite density at its centre or at the Big Bang; string theory is a candidate framework for unifying gravity with quantum mechanics, and the Standard Model is the established theory of fundamental particles and three of the four forces. All four belong to the physics of the cosmos and its constituents, so they arise in the context of observing and understanding the Universe. They have nothing to do with eclipse geometry, satellite launches or biological evolution.

items.value: All three uses are valid: genome sequencing identifies markers for disease resistance and drought tolerance, shortens varietal development, and helps decipher host-pathogen relationships
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: sequencing a crop genome allows molecular markers linked to traits such as disease resistance and drought tolerance to be located. Statement 2 is correct: with such markers, marker-assisted selection lets breeders screen seedlings in the laboratory rather than waiting for field expression over successive generations, cutting years off the development of a new variety. Statement 3 is correct: sequencing both the crop and its pathogen reveals the resistance and virulence genes on either side, which is exactly how host-pathogen interactions are dissected. All three are immediate, established applications, so D.

items.value: The main advantage of a parliamentary system is that the executive remains responsible to the legislature
items.reasoning: The defining feature and chief merit of the parliamentary form is responsible government: the council of ministers is drawn from and remains collectively answerable to the legislature, which can remove it at any time through a vote of no confidence, so accountability is continuous rather than periodic. The remaining options all describe the presidential form - separation of executive and legislature (A), continuity and efficiency arising from a fixed-term executive (B), and a head of government who can be replaced only at an election (D).

items.value: Rights and Duties are correlative - every right implies a corresponding duty
items.reasoning: Rights are claims recognised by society, and a claim is meaningless unless others are under a corresponding obligation to respect it; my right to free speech carries your duty not to silence me, and my right to property carries your duty not to take it. Indian constitutional practice reflects this, with Part III rights sitting alongside the Fundamental Duties added by the Forty-second Amendment. Option B is wrong because rights are conferred and protected by society and cannot be independent of it; options C and D are one-sided assertions that break the correlation the question is testing.

items.value: The Preamble reflects the mind of the makers of the Constitution
items.reasoning: The Preamble sets out the source of authority (We, the People of India), the nature of the polity (sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic), the objectives (justice, liberty, equality and fraternity) and the date of adoption, so it states in one place what the framers intended the Constitution to achieve. The Supreme Court has repeatedly described it in these terms, holding in In re Berubari Union that the Preamble is the key to open the mind of the makers. The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and Fundamental Duties each express only one part of that design.

items.value: Seven States - Nagaland, Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala
items.reasoning: Leaving Kohima, every road out of Nagaland towards the rest of India passes through Assam, and the only land route from the North East into the Indian mainland is the Siliguri corridor in West Bengal, so the first three States are fixed as Nagaland, Assam and West Bengal. Running south, West Bengal adjoins Odisha, Odisha adjoins Andhra Pradesh, and since Andhra Pradesh does not touch Kerala one southern State must intervene - either Tamil Nadu or Karnataka - before reaching Kerala. That gives a minimum of seven States including origin and destination, so the answer is B.

items.value: All three - adjournment motion, question hour and supplementary questions - are devices through which Parliament controls the Council of Ministers
items.reasoning: The adjournment motion sets aside the normal business of the House to debate a definite matter of urgent public importance and carries an element of censure of the government, so it is plainly an instrument of control. Question hour compels ministers to answer for the working of their departments on the floor of the House. Supplementary questions are the follow-ups a member may put after the ministerial reply, and they are often the sharpest part of the exercise because they cannot be prepared for in advance. All three are recognised parliamentary devices of executive accountability, so D.
